proposal.title: Oskiloyn: a library for aggregate statistics without raw data
proposal.summary: Oskiloyn builds a library for aggregate statistics without raw data for maintainers of public web services.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Usage statistics are often collected as raw personal data when aggregates would do. Maintainers of public web services depend on privacy-preserving measurement every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a library for aggregate statistics without raw data called Oskiloyn. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Privacy-preserving measurement is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/oskiloyn/oskiloyn. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 6 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 27100.00 EUR for 42 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Usage statistics are often collected as raw personal data when aggregates would do. Maintainers of public web services depend on privacy-preserving measurement every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a library for aggregate statistics without raw data called Oskiloyn. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Privacy-preserving measurement is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/oskiloyn/oskiloyn. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 6 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 27100.00 EUR for 42 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
